summary_1line: Duryodhana argues that kings must pursue success by any means and urges plotting against the Pandavas, while Dhritarashtra hesitates, fearing the disastrous consequences of hostility.

image_candidates.scene_text: Duryodhana stands before the blind king Dhritarashtra in the royal hall, passionately arguing that a king must seize prosperity even by deceit.
Sakuni holds dice in his hand like weapons while describing the dice-board as his chariot and the dice as arrows.
Dhritarashtra sits uneasy on his throne, warning that hostility will forge sharp swords and arrows of war.
